(1) lib/cms-mode.js exports three guard statements and a classifier:
- legacyGuardStatement(): INSERT INTO cms_state (id, mode, ...) SELECT 2, ... WHERE EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM cms_state WHERE id = 1 AND mode IS NOT 'legacy'). The EXISTS form means a table with no row reads as legacy, matching getCmsMode (lib/cms-mode.js:72-73). The CHECK(id = 1) failure aborts the batch.
- documentsGuardStatement(): aborts unless EXISTS(id = 1 AND mode = 'documents'). LIVEROW adds it to every documents publish, Undo and live-row batch.
- migratingGuardStatement(runId): aborts unless mode = 'migrating' AND a cms_migration_runs row with that id and finished_at IS NULL exists. Only lib/migrate/* uses it.
- Tenants without cms_state (before 0021): probe once (the hasRefsTable pattern: cache only a positive answer) and skip the legacy guard; the other two guards refuse on such tenants.
- classifyAbort(db, error, expectedMode): the CHECK text is identical to the release_state abort, so after any abort matching isGuardAbort it RE-READS cms_state.mode; if the mode is no longer the expected one it returns {kind: 'mode', mode}, otherwise {kind: 'lost'}. Message words: migrating -> 'Your store is being updated. Try again in a few minutes.'; documents -> today's STORE_USES_DOCUMENTS words.

- Source: the search_outbox rows P4-LIVEROW writes inside every live-row batch (publish, publishSet, Undo, undoSet, discardOrphanEdits), and that P4-CUTOVER (flip) and P4-REVERSE (reversal) write. A Reset changes only the draft; it reaches shoppers and search when that draft is published, through the same row.
- New lib/catalog/search-reindex.js: drainSearchOutbox({ client = null, limit = 100, log }) for the current tenant. It reads pending rows (rowid, product_id, handle) oldest first; reads the effective values with indexRows({ ids }) (P4-EFFECTIVE; do not edit effective.js); builds each document with buildSearchDoc and upserts them (documents().import with action 'upsert'); deletes by the stored handle a product that no longer exists (a null handle is marked done and left to the next full sync, which rebuilds the collection); then marks done only the rowids it read, so a row written meanwhile stays pending. It never drops or recreates the collection and never writes outside the current tenant's productsCollection(); with Typesense not configured or no namespace it makes no client call and marks the rows done. client defaults to getAdminClient(); tests pass a spy client, never a real Typesense.
- Triggers: (i) Fast path: lib/admin/documents-api.js, after a publish, publishSet, unpublish, undo, undoSet or discardOrphanEdits has answered success, calls kickSearchReindex() from search-reindex.js, which enqueues a durable 'search_reindex' job (enqueueDurable) and runs drainSearchOutbox inline with a short cap (SEARCH_REINDEX_TIMEOUT_MS, the same awaited-with-timeout pattern as lib/documents/after-commit.js, which stays unedited). A throw or timeout is logged ('search_reindex_failed' or 'search_reindex_timeout') and never changes the answer, because the publish is already live. The job idempotency key is 'search_reindex:' + tenantId() + ':' + the highest pending search_outbox rowid at kick time, so repeated kicks for the same pending rows coalesce but a later publish always gets a new job (jobs.idempotency_key is UNIQUE for all time and done jobs are kept for days, so a fixed per-tenant key would swallow every later kick); with no pending rows no job is enqueued. CUTOVER and REVERSE call the same kickSearchReindex(). (ii) Retry: a 'search_reindex' handler in lib/platform/worker.js HANDLERS runs drainSearchOutbox under the job's tenant; a failure throws into the job backoff. (iii) Backstop: every full sync drains the outbox after import ((1)), so rows left by a dead queue (enqueueDurable returns null), a store with no control plane or a failed fast path still converge.

(1) Preconditions, checked by the tool (not trusted to the runbook), each a plain refusal:
- the tenant ledger holds 0021 to 0025; no catalog sync_run is in progress; no pending schedule; mode is legacy (or migrating with an open run of this tool: resume);

(2) Steps, each recorded in cms_migration_runs (resumable from any step):
 a. Lock: one batch [legacyGuardStatement, set mode 'migrating', insert the cms_migration_runs row, with the live release id read at lock kept in its report JSON (0024 is pinned, so no new column)]. Catalog sync now parks (P4-GUARD); legacy writes refuse.
 b. Re-check pending schedule and live-read error AFTER the lock; a failure unlocks (mode back to legacy) and refuses.
 c. Backfill in chunks, every statement under migratingGuardStatement(run): documents UPSERT from the current legacy source (legacy wins: draft and published hashes from legacy; an existing different draft is first saved as a 'kept' version, counted in the report; update guarded by revision); versions with ON CONFLICT(id) DO NOTHING (content-addressed ids, so a conflict means the same body); refs via refRowsForBody; release:<id> rows via releaseRefRows for every retained release; product/collection live rows UPSERT of the legacy-derived columns only (modules, badge, pairs, pairs_title, layout_template, pinned) built with liveRowFor; title, description, gallery and display_* are never written here. Never INSERT OR IGNORE. After each chunk, verify row counts and ids exactly match the plan; any mismatch stops with a report.
 d. Data check (MIG-02, the hard gate): run the full lib/migrate/check.js (non-entity getters + entity getters reading back the backfilled live rows) through the SEAM, legacy source vs candidate. Any non-allowed difference unlocks and stops.
 e. Flip, one batch under migratingGuardStatement(run): insert the v4 release (rel_mig_), the pointer flip guarded on the pointer still equal to the live release id read at lock, migrated log rows, documents.published_*, any overlay columns being restored (REVERSE re-cutover only), search_outbox rows, cms_state mode 'documents' with cutover_release_id (the previous live release id or NULL), run step 'flipped'.

Build {versions, releaseId, now} with the doc_design version and call the after-commit entry (lib/documents/after-commit.js, imported, not edited) with the tenant context set (not _default) and a control-plane client; then RE-READ config.theme_pin, retry once, and report the result; resume redoes this step. Backfilled documents and legacy-derived live rows stay; legacy wins on the next run (2c), and shoppers never read them on a legacy store.
